rics.description: Policy Rates, Bank Rate
rics.meaning: PBoC Bank Rate — the 'rediscount rate' charged on bills the central bank discounts for commercial banks. Largely ceremonial post-2013 reforms; the LPR/MLF/OMO rates dominate active policy signaling.
rics.how_to_use: Slow-moving administrative rate. Used in some legacy financial contracts. Watch the gap to LPR for stance signals; sustained spread compression signals tighter policy regime.

rics.description: Policy Rates, RR1 - Reserve Requirement Ratio, Big Banks
rics.meaning: Reserve Requirement Ratio (RRR) for Big Banks — share of deposits that the largest Chinese banks must hold as reserves at the PBoC. Major monetary-policy tool: cuts release liquidity to the banking system; hikes drain it.
rics.how_to_use: Critical PBoC tool used to manage liquidity at quarterly and seasonal flow points. A 25 bp RRR cut typically releases ~CNY 500 billion of liquidity. Recent level ~9-10% (down from peak ~21% pre-2012). Cuts often signal dovish stance; markets watch announcement timing closely (typically late afternoon).

rics.description: Policy Rates, RR2 - Reserve Requirement Ratio - Small Banks
rics.meaning: Reserve Requirement Ratio, Small Banks — RRR applied to smaller financial institutions. Set 50-100 bps below the big-bank RRR to support SME lending.
rics.how_to_use: Tiered RRR is a targeted-easing tool. Differential cuts (only small-bank RRR cut) signal targeted SME-support stance. Watch the spread between big-bank and small-bank RRR for tiered-policy signals.

rics.description: 金融机构活期储蓄存款利率(年率化)_全国
rics.meaning: China regional / sectoral statistic: 金融机构活期储蓄存款利率(年率化)_全国. Detailed regional or sectoral data series — original Chinese description preserved.
rics.how_to_use: Refer to source description for specific content. Regional and city-level data in the China dataset captures provincial and urban-level economic activity, often used by analysts tracking specific localities.

rics.description: Average lending rate, bill financing
rics.meaning: Average Lending Rate, Bill Financing — rate on short-term commercial bills (banker's acceptances) financed by banks. Most rate-sensitive lending segment.
rics.how_to_use: Bill rates are among the most-watched short-term financing indicators in China. Sharp drops indicate banks meeting lending quotas via bill discounting (low-quality 'window dressing'). PBoC and CBIRC monitor for evidence of low-quality credit creation.

rics.description: Average lending rate, individual mortgage loans
rics.meaning: Average Lending Rate, Individual Mortgage Loans — weighted average new-mortgage rate. Set as LPR-5Y plus a regulator-determined spread (positive for additional homes).
rics.how_to_use: Tracks the property-cycle credit channel. China cut individual-mortgage rates aggressively 2022-24 (from peak ~5.6% to ~3.3%) to support property demand. Watch the spread to 5Y LPR — narrowing spread signals support; wider spread signals tightening.

rics.description: Policy Rates, 20 Day Reloan Rate
rics.meaning: PBoC 20-Day Reloan Rate — the rate at which the PBoC lends to commercial banks for 20-day terms. Used in PBoC's open market operations alongside the 7-day reverse repo rate.
rics.how_to_use: Niche; the 7-day reverse repo (separate series, sometimes published) is more market-relevant. Reloan-rate moves signal targeted liquidity provision to specific bank categories.

rics.description: Policy Rates, Deposit Rate, 1 Year, The Peoples Bank of China
rics.meaning: PBoC 1-Year Benchmark Deposit Rate — administrative deposit rate that anchors household deposit pricing at Chinese banks. Less actively used since the LPR reform but still publicly cited.
rics.how_to_use: Pre-2015 the headline policy rate; now overshadowed by LPR. Banks have flexibility to price above this floor. Sustained sub-1.5% reflects the post-2020 disinflation/deflation regime. Used to gauge implicit financial-repression of household savers.

rics.description: Policy Rates, Deposit rate, 1 year
rics.meaning: 1-Year Deposit Rate — alternative release of the 1Y benchmark deposit rate.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against aCNDEPR1Y. Banks have flexibility to price above this benchmark floor.

rics.description: Policy Rates, Loan Prime Rate 1Y, The Peoples Bank of China
rics.meaning: 1-Year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) — the People's Bank of China's primary policy lending benchmark since the August 2019 reform that pegged it to the medium-term lending facility (MLF) rate plus a contributing-bank-determined spread. Set monthly on the 20th by 18 quoting banks.
rics.how_to_use: THE key China lending-rate benchmark. Used to price most corporate loans. PBoC signals through the MLF rate and lets the LPR move with it. A 5-10 bp cut typically triggers analyst headlines and CNY/equity reaction. Recent range 3.10-3.85%. Pair with the 5Y LPR (aCNLPR5YRR) which is the mortgage-pricing benchmark.

rics.description: Policy Rates, Loan Prime Rate 5Y, The Peoples Bank of China
rics.meaning: 5-Year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) — the longer-tenor LPR that serves as the benchmark for individual mortgage rates and longer-duration corporate loans. Set monthly alongside the 1Y LPR.
rics.how_to_use: THE mortgage-rate benchmark. PBoC has used asymmetric cuts (5Y > 1Y) to support real estate without easing too aggressively for short-term lending. The 5Y has been cut harder than the 1Y in 2022-24 to support the property sector. Watch the 5Y-1Y spread for the property-policy stance.

rics.description: Policy Rates, Major Loan Rate, Financial Institutions, 1 Year & Below
rics.meaning: Major Loan Rate, Financial Institutions, 1 Year & Below — average lending rate on loans up to 1 year extended by Chinese financial institutions. Aggregates LPR-pricing across the system.
rics.how_to_use: Captures effective lending costs (vs LPR which is the benchmark). The spread vs LPR signals risk-premium dynamics — widening spreads suggest banks pricing in greater credit risk.

rics.description: Reserve Requirement Ratio, Big Banks
rics.meaning: Reserve Requirement Ratio, Big Banks — same conceptual measure as aCNCRR in alternative framing.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary release. Use whichever has fresher data; methodology and timing differences across releases are typically minor and resolved on revision.

rics.description: average lending rate, ordinary loans
rics.meaning: Average Lending Rate, Ordinary Loans — weighted average rate on ordinary (non-bill, non-mortgage) bank loans. Subset of the broader weighted-average lending rate.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner signal of corporate-loan pricing than the broad weighted average. Watch the spread vs LPR for credit-risk premium dynamics.

rics.description: weighted average leading rate
rics.meaning: Weighted Average Lending Rate (general) — the headline blended lending rate published by the PBoC quarterly. Captures the rate at which Chinese banks actually extended new loans.
rics.how_to_use: Most analytically useful 'real economy' lending-rate gauge — includes regulatory pricing pressures and bank competitive dynamics. Sustained declines despite stable LPR signal banks competing for lending share. PBoC cites this in Monetary Policy Reports.
